observations: Model states one hundred fixed cost plus two per widget; prediction asks incremental cost of widget fifty-one.
At fifty, total two hundred and average four; adding one changed total to 202 and average 3.96.
At one hundred, total three hundred and average three while next-unit cost remained two.
Screenshot contrasts descending average-cost curve with flat marginal-cost line. Reveal recalls fifty-to-fifty-one and adds a three-dollar extra-order example with capacity-cost caveat.

complexity.reason: Distinguishes total, average and marginal quantities.
complexity.conceptualDemand: Avoid assigning historical fixed costs to the next decision.

whyCool: The next unit can cost less than the average because it does not bring the fixed costs all over again.
caveat: Constant variable-cost model with no capacity step or demand effects.
effort: Prediction, fifty baseline, fifty-one increment, hundred-unit boundary, screenshot and reveal.
bucketReason: Clear dual-curve mechanism and concrete conditional transfer.

prediction.reason: A useful distinction but the stated per-widget cost directly supplies the answer.
prediction.evidence: Two per widget versus average four.

interaction.reason: Original discrete increment and output boundary separate average from marginal cost.
interaction.evidence: Fifty, fifty-one and one hundred with fixed next-unit cost.

payoff.reason: Explains observed total change, fixed-cost allocation and a concrete incremental decision limit.
payoff.evidence: Three-dollar extra order adds one here; real costs may rise with capacity.

clarity.reason: Curve and horizontal line make quantities distinct.
clarity.evidence: Average 3.96 versus next one plus two.

transfer.reason: Concrete new-use example and applicability condition.
transfer.evidence: Extra order below average can contribute if fixed costs do not rise; busy workshop limit.

surprise.reason: A price below average cost can still add profit at the margin.
surprise.evidence: Three-dollar additional order versus four average.

visualExplanation.reason: Two different curve shapes expose why averages and increments diverge.
visualExplanation.evidence: Descending average versus flat marginal line across output.

playfulness.evidence: Discrete original increment and larger production tested.

practicalValue.evidence: Additional order contribution under fixed-cost assumption.

depth.reason: Fixed cost dilution, marginal cost and contribution connect.
depth.evidence: Average falls while incremental cost stays constant.
